stem: What is the primary clinical limitation of the maternal intrapartum antimicrobial prophylaxis used for Group B \textit{Streptococcus} (GBS)?

options.text: It is only 20% effective against early onset sepsis.
It has no measurable effect on the incidence of late onset GBS sepsis.
It increases the risk of neonatal herpes simplex virus transmission.
It requires screening to be done in the first trimester to be effective.

explanation: While it significantly reduces colonization and early infection, it does not prevent the development of GBS sepsis occurring after the first week of life.
rationale: Focus on the specific timing of the infection that the treatment fails to prevent.

optionExplanations.A: The prophylaxis is actually highly effective, reducing the incidence of early onset disease by approximately 80%.
optionExplanations.B: While it significantly reduces colonization and early infection, it does not prevent the development of GBS sepsis occurring after the first week of life.
optionExplanations.C: There is no evidence suggesting that GBS antibiotic prophylaxis impacts the transmission rates of viral infections like HSV.
optionExplanations.D: Screening is more protective when performed later in the pregnancy rather than early on.

source.hint: Focus on the specific timing of the infection that the treatment fails to prevent.
